# Questions for the client — Imani Reyes-Okafor (2026-10-08)

Answers to items 1–4 change the analysis, not just the numbers. Please answer in order; "I don't know / not in my file" is a useful answer.

## A. The agreement (highest priority)

1. **Do you have the complete Amended and Restated Operating Agreement — not the five excerpts we were given?** We need every section, especially: the **exact dilution formula** in or referenced by §6.3 (a table, a defined "Percentage Interest" recalculation, or an example); any **notice/article** section (does it allow email, hand delivery, or text, or say notice is "deemed delivered" when sent?); any **member-level** waiver of duties (the excerpted §7.3 waives only "the Manager's" duties); whether the Manager can **amend** the agreement alone or with a majority vote; withdrawal and transfer rights; any **arbitration**, fee-shifting, or shortened limitations period; and any **indemnification/advancement** provision.
2. Were you ever asked to sign a **consent, waiver, ratification, or annual certification** that disclosed or approved the Castellan engagement, the capital call, or the dilution? (Anything signed destroys the tolling argument.)
3. Has the agreement been amended since you joined, and were you asked to approve amendments?

## B. The capital call and the $1,500,000

4. **How was the $1,500,000 actually spent?** Do you have bank statements or a receipts-and-uses ledger? Specifically: was any of it used to pay Castellan Asset Services fees, repay a loan from Bram, fund acquisitions, or sit in the account? Was the Company short of cash in August 2026 (were operating distributions stopped, were vendors late, was there a loan covenant problem)?
5. **How was Bram's payment of your $270,000 recorded** — as his capital contribution, a loan to you, or an advance? Was any note, interest rate, or offset against your interest created or mentioned?
6. When did you first learn of the capital call (exact date and channel)? Did you reply to the text, ask for an extension, or offer to fund part of it? Did anyone from the Company respond?
7. What is your **current mailing address and email**, and had you given the Company that address before 2026-08-20? Which address and email are in the Company's records, and who maintains them? Has certified mail ever reached you?

## C. The fees and the affiliate arrangement

8. **What were the Company's gross rents for 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025 and 2026-to-date?** (Needed to compute the monthly 6% property-management fee, which is not quantified anywhere in the file — today every fee total we state covers only the $1,050,000 of "asset management fee.")
9. What do you know, or can you get, about **market rates** for third-party property management and asset management on comparable properties? (The §5.4 fairness condition turns on arm's-length comparables.)
10. Do you have any **Castellan engagement agreement, invoice, or the 2022-08-15 resolution** itself? Any written disclosure of any kind, ever — even an email, an annual report line item, a K-1 footnote, or a conversation?
11. **When exactly in 2026 did you learn of the arrangement**, and what triggered it (a document you received, a tax form, a conversation)? When did you request records from the Manager, and when were they produced? This is the whole tolling case for the $375,000 of 2022–2023 fees.
12. The minutes say the asset fee was $180,000/yr "escalating 8%/yr," but the payments rose by exactly $15,000/yr. Do you know of any amendment, side letter, or side agreement changing that fee?

## D. Valuation

13. Who prepared the broker opinion (name, credential), was it a **formal appraisal**, what **standard of value** was used, and is there a written report we can attach? Is the $14.5M enterprise / $9.8M equity derived from a rent roll and cap rate, or a comparable-sales approach?
14. Do you have the **2025 year-end balance sheet** behind the $3,100,000 members' equity figure? What real estate is on the books, at what cost, and how much accumulated depreciation and debt? Was the $3.1M prepared by Bram, and was it ever audited or appraised?
15. Does the Company have any **recent appraisal, refinancing valuation, insurance replacement value, or a pending third-party offer** for the property?
16. Did the Manager produce **any computation** for the $7,200,000 "fair value" or for **how 6.1% was calculated**? We cannot reproduce 6.1% from $7,200,000 under any pro rata formula (value-weighted gives 14.90%; book-weighted 12.13%; exactly 6.1% implies a fair value of $768,908), so either the Manager used a formula we have not seen or the number is arbitrary — we need to know which.
17. Has the Company **ever distributed cash** to you, and what is your understanding of your exit rights?

## E. Procedural posture

18. Has any lawyer written to the Company on your behalf, and has the Company acknowledged or extended the 30-day offer window (it appears to expire **2026-10-31**)?
19. Did you **guarantee any Company debt** or sign any personal obligation? Any exposure we need to protect you from?
20. What is your **realistic cash situation and time horizon** — can you fund any litigation costs at all, and do you need cash within 12 months? (This drives whether we structure a settlement as cash now versus a secured note.)
21. Have you done anything that could be read as **accepting the 6.1%** — accepting a 6.1% K-1, voting at a meeting by 6.1%, or corresponding with the Company about your "6.1% interest"?

He texted me a PDF on August 20. No letter. My email on file is from 2019 and dead. I saw the text but assumed it wasn't real notice.
I only saw the affiliate fees in 2026 when I finally got the bank statements through a books-and-records demand. Before that I got one-page summaries with 'management expenses'.
I can't raise $270k. Maybe $60k.
